E1.evidence: Issue #783 gives a reproduction ("if i keep refreshing my webpage, it eventually crashes rosbridge server") and a launch log ending in "[ERROR] [rosbridge_websocket-1]: process has died [pid 75242, exit code -11, ..." (rosbridge 1.2.0, Foxy); merged PR #803 says "Fixes #783" and a maintainer (zflat) confirmed "I did a quick test locally to confirm that these changes address the issues seen in https://github.com/RobotWebTools/rosbridge_suite/issues/783".

units_identified: web client (reporter's webpage over the rosbridge WebSocket protocol)
E2.evidence: The defect is a concurrency fault inside rosbridge's own multi-client subscription bookkeeping and would occur with any correct WebSocket client that connects, subscribes and disconnects quickly. PR #803: "This PR improves multi-client connection robustness by - avoiding unregistering of subscribers if one client disconnects while all others are still waiting for the [initial callback](...) - avoiding a deadlock that could occur when new clients connect, subscribe to a topic and then immediately disconnect again". A related symptom found during review was also internal: "RuntimeError: dictionary changed size during iteration" with the explanation "we only create a reference to the callbacks, not a deep copy" (achim-k, PR #803). No value, frame, name, or timing assumption between the client and the server is wrong; the client uses the protocol correctly (standard subscribe ops). The reporter's segfault has no stack trace; the reporter asked whether a tornado version mismatch was involved, but no source confirms a tornado or rclpy version mismatch as the cause. PR #803 (supersedes #741, also fixes #758) was merged into ros2 on 2022-10-17 as fada151f45bcfd68483a369684a0aa0a80d180ca; an intermittent tornado WebSocketClosedError trace seen during review was downgraded to a warning.

E3.evidence: Not evaluated past E2. The triggering pattern is repeated SWITCH/CONCURRENT client sessions (disconnect and reconnect of the page), but the failure is inside rosbridge_server.

E4.evidence: Observed crash: "process has died [pid 75242, exit code -11, ..." in the issue log.

ineligible_reason: internal: deadlock and unsynchronized callback-dictionary handling inside rosbridge_library/rosbridge_server when several WebSocket clients connect, subscribe and disconnect in quick succession; the fix (PR #803) replaces the Lock with an RLock, holds it across the callback loop, counts pending new subscriptions in has_subscribers(), destroys the pending new subscriber on unregister, and stops re-raising WebSocketClosedError. The crash would occur with any correct client.
